name: P2-practo
prompt: Below are 6 numbered screenshots of the Practo mobile app (Android) captured by the owner as a DESIGN REFERENCE (call them P1..P6 in the order provided). For EACH screenshot: (1) identify the screen (home, search, doctor listing, doctor profile, clinic/hospital page, booking flow, filters, orders, chat, health hub, account, etc.), (2) describe its visual design in depth: layout structure, list/card design, PHOTO usage (are doctor/clinic photos shown? circular avatars? sizes?), typography hierarchy (sizes/weights), the color system (what reads as primary vs secondary/accent color; approximate hex), components (chips, badges, pills, tabs, bottom nav, ratings, buttons, banners), spacing/density feel, (3) name the ONE design element that most makes this screen feel premium/desirable. This informs a redesign of another Indian healthcare booking app, so extract transferable patterns. Be concrete and honest.
verdict:
# Practo App — Screen-by-Screen Design Analysis

## P1 — Home (top half): Search + Specialty Tiles + Free Expert Q&A

**Screen ID:** Home feed, mid-scroll.

**Layout:** Vertical stack: sticky pill search bar ("Search for Clinics and...") + a bordered "Ask Care AI" pill button at top-right; horizontal carousel of specialty tiles (Dentist, Eye Specialist, ENT) with photographic headers fading into white label area; section header "Free Expert Q&A" with a blue "Explore all ›" link; horizontally-swipeable Q&A cards; a soft CTA banner ("Got a health query?" + orange "Free" pill + circular blue arrow button); partial view of a stats section.

**Cards:** Q&A card = large white rounded card (~24px radius) on a pale lavender (#ECEBFA-ish) background. Inside: circular pale-blue icon avatar (community/users glyph), bold title "Community Question", grey "16h ago", a mint-green pill badge "Answered" (green text ~#1B7A3D on #D8F2DF), an inset white quote block with large ~22px dark text of the question, then a row of overlapping circular doctor photos with a "+4" blue count circle, and a footer row divided by hairline: eye icon + "23" views, share icon + "Share".

**Photos:** Real photos here are (a) background imagery on specialty tiles (cropped clinical photos, ~120px tall, rounded), (b) small ~40px circular stacked avatars of answering doctors. Not portrait-heavy — photos are contextual.

**Typography:** Bold black section title (~26px); card title semibold ~18px; question text large, near-black, generous line-height; meta text grey #8A8A9E ~14px. Clear 3-level hierarchy.

**Color:** Primary = Practo blue/indigo (#3D5AFE / brand deep blue #2B2E8C in logo, bottom nav active circle #3B3FC4). Secondary/accent = orange (#F5A623 "Free" pill), mint green badge, lavender page background. White cards carry everything.

**Components:** Pill search, AI pill (white with blue gradient border + sparkle), green status badge, overlapping avatar stack, footer-metric row, floating rounded bottom nav.

**Density:** Airy — big paddings (~20px), soft elevation shadows, nothing cramped.

**Premium element:** The **layered white Q&A card with the green "Answered" pill and stacked doctor avatars** — it makes community answers feel verified and alive, which reads as trust = premium.

---

## P2 — Home (bottom): Trust Stats + Brand Sign-off

**Screen ID:** Still home, footer region.

**Layout:** Same "Got a health query?" banner, then a huge white rounded panel containing a centered stats stack: "5 Lakh+ / DOCTORS", "30 Crore+ / USERS", "2.5 Lakh+ / ESTABLISHMENTS REGISTERED", ending with the ".practo." logo lockup. Floating pill bottom nav overlaps it.

**Typography:** This is the star — enormous extra-bold numerals (~56px, near-black #1C1C28) with wide-tracked uppercase small labels (~16px, letter-spaced). Monumental, editorial scale contrast.

**Color:** Pure white panel on lavender bg; logo deep indigo #2B2E8C with sky-blue dots.

**Components:** Floating bottom nav — white pill container, active "Home" as a large solid indigo circle with white icon, inactive items as thin-line icons with tiny labels (In-Person, Video Consult, Account).

**Density:** Extremely generous; vertical whitespace does the work.

**Premium element:** The **billboard-scale trust numbers with letter-spaced caps labels** — turning metrics into brand theatre. Highly transferable: a "social proof as typography" moment near the home footer.

---

## P3 — Find Doctors (Specialty Browse / Search Landing)

**Screen ID:** Search/discovery landing for the doctors vertical (not yet a listing).

**Layout:** Solid deep-indigo app bar (#2E3192) with back arrow, bold white "Find Doctors", city selector "Bangalore ⌄" on right. Below: white helper strip with orange "?" badge — "Learn how to book an appointment ›"; large grey pill search ("Search Symptoms/ Specialities"); section "Most searched specialities" as a 4×2 grid of illustrated circular icons (~72px) with labels; outlined full-width "View All Specialities" button; start of "Conditions treated through surgeries" section.

**Photos:** No photography — flat vector illustrations in a consistent coral (#F2795F) + purple (#5B3E96) + pale-blue-circle palette. Consistency of illustration style is itself the design system.

**Typography:** Dark-grey section headers ~28px bold; labels ~17px regular, dark grey, centered under icons; helper text medium.

**Color:** Indigo header as the anchor of a mostly white page; orange used sparingly as attention accent.

**Components:** App bar with city switcher, help strip, oversized pill search, icon grid, outline CTA button.

**Density:** Comfortable; icon grid is evenly spaced, labels wrap to two lines.

**Premium element:** The **solid deep-indigo header with integrated city selector** — instant "official product" feel and spatial orientation, versus the white floaty home.

---

## P4 — Find Doctors (Surgeries + Symptoms Grids)

**Screen ID:** Same Find Doctors flow, scrolled: surgery conditions grid + "Most common symptoms" grid.

**Layout:** Pure 4-column icon-grid scrolling page; two bold section headers with grey subcopy ("Find top surgeons near you...").

**Cards/Icons:** Same 72px circular pale-blue-gradient tiles with coral/purple flat illustrations (Piles, Hernia, Kidney Stone, COVID, Fever...). Labels centered, truncate with ellipsis ("Appendicitis", "Circumcisio n") — an honest flaw: long labels break awkwardly, no chip fallback.

**Typography:** Identical system to P3 — consistent header scale keeps rhythm across a long scroll.

**Color:** Restraint: white + grey text + the two-tone illustration palette; no cards, no borders — grid floats on white.

**Density:** Moderate; whitespace between sections is large (~40px), grid gaps tight.

**Premium element:** The **unified illustrated icon language** — one style, one palette across ~20 medical categories. This consistency is what makes the catalog feel curated rather than stocky.

---

## P5 — Find Doctors (Categories Cards)

**Screen ID:** Same vertical, "Categories" section — 2-column content cards.

**Layout:** Header "Categories"; 2-column grid of large cards: big rounded illustration banner (16:10, gradient pale-blue bg, ~340px wide), then bold title ("Skin and hair", "Women's health", "Chronic problems", "Bone and joint", "Sexual health") and 3-line grey description, clamped with ellipsis.

**Photos:** No photos — large editorial illustrations, effectively hero images per category.

**Typography:** Card titles bold ~24px dark; descriptions ~17px grey #55555E; the banner-image → title → body stack mirrors editorial/magazine cards.

**Color:** Same coral/purple/indigo system; card backgrounds are subtle gradient washes, no borders or shadows — separation is purely from spacing.

**Density:** The airiest screen yet; two cards per row with big gutters.

**Premium element:** **Gradient illustration banners acting as hero images** — gives each medical category editorial weight without relying on inconsistent clinic stock photos.

---

## P6 — Find Doctors (Testimonials + All Specialities)

**Screen ID:** Same vertical, footer: "What patient's say" carousel + "All specialities" complete grid.

**Layout:** Testimonial card (white, rounded, thin grey border, swipeable — page dots below): circular illustrated avatar, bold name "Barunabh Ghosh", grey "1 week ago", multi-line review text. Then "All specialities" 4-column grid reusing the circular illustration tiles (COVID, Skin & Hair... "Digesitve Issues" — note the typo and "Homeopath y" wrap, real polish gaps).

**Photos:** Illustrated avatars instead of user photos — privacy-appropriate and stylistically consistent.

**Typography:** Section headers identical to P3–P5; review text ~18px with relaxed line-height, reads like a quote.

**Color:** Same system; testimonial card is the only bordered component on the page.

**Components:** Carousel + dot indicator, bordered quote card, icon grid.

**Premium element:** **Social proof placed as a designed, bordered testimonial card directly inside the discovery funnel** — reassurance at the exact moment of decision, with the dots signaling a living community.

---

## Transferable Patterns (for the redesign)

1. **Two-mode color strategy:** soft lavender/white "assistant" home vs solid indigo (#2E3192) headers for task-verticals — signals context switch instantly.
2. **Consistent illustrated icon system** (coral + purple on pale-blue circles) for medical taxonomy — avoids the stock-photo mess typical of Indian health apps; reserve real photos for doctors/answers only.
3. **Typography as trust:** giant bold stats + letter-spaced caps labels for social proof; 3-level text hierarchy everywhere (28 bold / 18 medium / 14 grey).
4. **Verification badges** ("Answered" mint pill, "Free" orange pill) — small colored pills carry enormous credibility weight.
5. **Floating pill bottom nav** with a filled circular active state.
6. **Social proof mid-funnel** (testimonials in the discovery flow, not just on profiles).
7. **Honest flaws to avoid:** label truncation in 4-col grids ("Circumcisio n", "Digesitve Issues"), no doctor photos on home creating coldness in the booking funnel itself.
